key_insight: This paper shows that generative modeling can be driven by a distributional energy that creates direct sample-level motion, enabling a one-step generator without relying on adversarial critics, handcrafted noise paths, or autoregressive factorization. The proposed Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM) converts energy distance into simple per-sample interactions that supervise generation directly.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of generating realistic samples without unstable adversarial training, complicated diffusion-style trajectories, or sequential autoregressive dependencies. The goal is a simpler, direct way to train generators using distribution-level supervision.
method: Uses a proper distributional energy to induce motion at the sample level, rather than relying on a discriminator or multi-step path.
Implements Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM), where each generated sample interacts with one real source and one independent repulsive source.
Transforms energy distance into a constant-size interaction per projectile, providing direct regression targets for a one-step generator.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a potentially simpler and more stable generative training paradigm with direct supervision and fewer moving parts. It may reduce training complexity while preserving strong distribution-matching behavior.
